claims.text: A calibrated in-situ thermal-feedback system can dynamically modulate laser power during selective laser melting of CoCrFeNiMn.
Dynamic laser-power modulation will improve the dimensional precision of SLM-produced CoCrFeNiMn components.
Dynamic laser-power modulation will improve the mechanical integrity of SLM-produced CoCrFeNiMn components.
Dynamic laser-power modulation will reduce fabrication-induced thermal gradients.
Reducing local thermal gradients will homogenize the melt pool.
Reducing local thermal gradients will produce a more uniform solidification front.
Continuous adjustment of laser power and dwell time can maintain a consistent melt-pool temperature profile.
Rapid thermal fluctuations contribute to residual stresses in SLM components.
Rapid thermal fluctuations contribute to microstructural heterogeneity in SLM components.
Rapid thermal fluctuations contribute to porosity and micro-cracking in SLM components.
Mitigating thermal fluctuations will enhance dimensional precision.
Mitigating thermal fluctuations will enhance mechanical integrity.
Feedback-controlled components will have a lower defect density than components made by conventional SLM.
Feedback-controlled components will have greater tensile strength than components made by conventional SLM.
Feedback-controlled components will have greater ductility than components made by conventional SLM.
Conventional SLM of CoCrFeNiMn without real-time thermal modulation has variable thermal gradients, higher defect densities, and less consistent mechanical properties.
The expected improvement depends on the response speed and accuracy of the thermal-feedback system.
The intervention may require additional calibration before it can be extrapolated to other alloy systems or machine setups.
